name: Website fingerprinting on real websites (pilot)
status: pilot: 20 monitored sites, closed and open world; not literature scale

setup.where: GCP n2-standard-4, europe-west4-a, user-namespace lab with live internet (pasta)
setup.browser: headless Firefox ESR via Selenium, fresh profile per load
setup.capture: the client's carrier (what an ISP or Wi-Fi sees), AF_PACKET, GSO super-frames split into wire packets
setup.sites: 20 monitored Tranco sites x ~30 loads, plus 300 unmonitored sites once each (open world)
setup.validity_gate: an attack's result on a defence is reported only if it reaches 80% closed-world on the undefended baseline

undefended.reading: every attack passes the validity gate: the lab can recognise real websites

fast.reading: k-FP 14.8% closed world (chance 5%) and an open-world true-positive rate near zero: far from the baseline, but above chance; see cpu_contention

metered.reading: at chance, but only 31 of 900 loads completed normally: metered (~0.3 Mbit/s of application throughput) is too slow for browsing today's websites and is not a browsing class

results.not_run: DF and Tik-Tok on fast and metered (k-FP only)

cpu_contention.question: does fast stay near chance when the browser competes with the client's data plane for CPU, as on a laptop?
cpu_contention.setup: same lab and shape; browser and client data plane pinned to the same 2 cores (relay and exit on the other 2); 20 monitored sites x 10 loads; compared with the pilot runs cut to the same 20 sites x 10 loads (mean of 5 random draws)
cpu_contention.mechanism: the shaper's grid skips ticks it misses ('skipped, never burst'), so under CPU load the pattern of missed ticks follows the page's own work

results.variant: fast, browser not pinned with the data plane (pilot)
a: fast, shared cores, today's code
b: a + data plane at nice -10

cpu_contention.reading: under CPU contention fast leaks strongly (81%); priority barely helps; catch-up halves the leak but leaves it ten times chance. The catch-up stays an off-by-default experiment (AVPN_CATCH_UP_MS, default 0), and fast is not claimed to resist website fingerprinting on a busy CPU

open: the leak needs a fix that removes the timing signal itself (for example a shaper whose sends do not depend on the host keeping up), proved by this same contention run
